notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The ayah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant.
He made their plot go astray.
He sent birds in flocks upon them.
The birds struck them with stones of sijjil.
He made them like chaff that has been eaten.

chapters.summary_md: The surah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant, and says He made their plot go astray [c1][c2]. He sent birds in flocks upon them, which struck them with stones, and made them like chaff that has been eaten [c3][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant [c1]. He made their plot go astray [c2].

He sent birds in flocks upon them [c3]. The birds struck them with stones of sijjil [c4]. He made them like chaff that has been eaten [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The account is a few short ayat and is built as questions followed by what God did [c1][c2]. The word sijjil is left untranslated here, and the word for flocks is read in more than one way [c3][c4]. The last ayah describes the result with a comparison to chaff that has been eaten [c5].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat ask if you have seen what the Lord did to the companions of the elephant [c1]. He made their plot go wrong, sent flocks of birds with stones, and made them like eaten chaff [c2][c3][c4][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show a plot that went astray [c2]. Another is that the account is told as something the hearer is asked to consider [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the companions of the elephant were, where they went, what their plot was, or when this happened; the ayat give only the title and what God did.
- Not established: how many there were, how many elephants, or what became of them beyond the comparison to chaff.
- Not established: what the birds were, how many, or what the stones of sijjil were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the leader, the kingdom he came from, the place he marched against and the year of the event.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, and early historical reports on who the companions of the elephant were and when. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the leader Abraha, the land of Yemen, and the place they marched against.
The words sijjil and ababil are rendered plainly or left untranslated; a scholar should decide how the page should word them.
